subject: Decision Making
subcategory: The Science of Risk and Reward
title: Sunk Cost in Investing
description: A micro-lesson that makes Sunk Cost in Investing usable.

hook.text: You bought a stock at $100. It is now $50. You hold on, hoping to break even. The original price should not matter.

buildup.text: Sunk costs are gone forever. Rational decisions consider only future expected returns, not past money already spent.

discovery.text: The Concorde jet was a famous sunk cost trap. Britain and France kept funding it long after it was clear it would lose.

twist.text: Sunk cost thinking extends beyond money. People stay in bad jobs and relationships because of time already invested.

climax.text: The sunk cost fallacy makes us throw good resources after bad.

punchline.text: Money already lost is gone. Decide based on the future, not on past investments.

quiz.question: How should you evaluate a losing investment rationally?
options: Ignore the purchase price and ask whether you would buy it today at the current price
